corrections.reason: g2-soc-photo-map-info already depends on g2-soc-continents-oceans through g2-soc-location-climate, so listing continents-oceans directly is redundant under the direct-prerequisite rule. Keeping only g2-soc-photo-map-info still covers the continent and ocean knowledge transitively.

The skill asks kids to compare young people from different backgrounds (wealthy, poor, slave, and so on), but nothing in the current list teaches those social groups. g4-soc-group-daily-lives covers how different groups in society lived, which is the missing direct prerequisite. g4-soc-daily-life already reaches the kid through g4-soc-group-daily-lives (via g4-soc-compare-organization and g4-soc-social-organization), so it is removed as redundant.

The skill compares seasonal rhythms and land use, and the seasonal and natural-process knowledge comes from g4-soc-physical-features, which was missing. g2-soc-sustainability is already a dependency of g4-soc-physical-features, so listing it directly is redundant under the direct-prerequisite rule.

g3-soc-make-ontario-maps already depends on g2-soc-cardinal-directions transitively (through g3-soc-landform-regions, g2-soc-photo-map-info, and g2-soc-location-climate), so listing cardinal directions directly is redundant. The map-making skill still covers the direct route to this one.

This skill asks kids to pick responsible resource actions, which is the same idea as the grade 2 skill g2-soc-sustainability (Using Nature Carefully). None of the existing prerequisite chain reaches that skill, so it was missing.

output.notes: Reviewed all 15 proposed Grade 4 skills against the prerequisite rules. Five skills need corrections. Several prerequisites were removed because another listed prerequisite already depends on them through the chain; the rule is applied literally. Two skills (g4-soc-young-people and g4-soc-environment-compare) gained a direct prerequisite that the kid needs for the expectation. The g4-soc-sustainable-actions skill was missing the grade 2 sustainability idea. The remaining skills look correct on prerequisites, titles, and descriptions, and their wording suits reading aloud.
